title: Weight-Space Programming Changes How an LLM Uses Python for Computational Biology
abstract: arXiv:2611.20566v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Weight-space programming allows a language model to edit another model's weights without gradient-based training. We used Claude Opus 5.5 to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B and investigated how the edits changed its use of Python on computational biology problems. We compared four initial edited checkpoints with the original model on 50 test problems across three test seeds, yielding 600 paired evaluations. Strictly correct answers increased from 44 to 77, and technically correct answers, which included correct final values rejected for formatting, increased from 64 to 100. Repeated Python calls decreased from 1,834 to 1,044. Among the 64 pairs in which only the edited response was technically correct, the original model had already computed the correct value in 36 but did not submit a technically correct final answer. tldr: 利用权重空间编程让Claude Opus 5.5直接编辑Qwen3.5-0.8B的权重（无需梯度训练），显著提升了小模型在计算生物学任务中用Python解题的正确率（严格正确答案从44增至77），并大幅减少了冗余的Python调用。
